texts: bad: "the Keepers" is a capitalized plural kind-word label, the one spot where the translator is genuinely unstable — here it became a group whose members are keepers, which the rules forbid for such a label, and the group reading then owed a per-member rule that was never emitted (the same phrase in L2-20 went the other way, as a single named body). The small-clause attitude "considers X sacred" is also an unlegislated shape; only the finite that-clause form is specified. Write "Every Keeper considers that lantern-tending is sacred." — the singular "Keeper" under an explicit universal ranges over the keeper kind with no label ambiguity, and the that-clause is the attitude shape the instruction set actually covers.
good. the "not" lands as a strength-0 denial on the same kind-level property atom, the compound "lantern-tending" decomposes cleanly, and nothing false is asserted.

bad: "there are no Ns" has no licensed non-existence form, so the parse denied a bundle over one freshly minted witness — it says one unspecified thing is not a formal prayer, not that no formal prayers exist; the universal force of "no" is lost. Write "No prayer is formal." — the ordinary generic denial (strength 0 on the kind-level atom, with the quantifier word "no" recorded), which is truth-conditionally the same non-existence claim and is fully specified.
good. two clean events joined by "while" (the counting nested inside the trimming), and repeating the full name instead of a pronoun is exactly what keeps both clauses on one symbol.

good. "each evening" yields the evening slot plus its implied daily cycle, the iron bands are typed and attached to the lantern as parts, and the named lantern gets its kind atom — all participants covered.
